text:
Everything above assumes that the “hostile presence” is symbolic, the kind that settles down when you ground yourself and meet it with love. What you’re going through might instead be psychosis, or your mind becoming unstable in some other way.

Get help right away if you feel under attack for days at a time, or you can’t sleep or function normally. The same goes if you hear voices telling you to do things, feel you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, or feel you’re going manic. And get help if you can’t communicate normally, or can’t tell the difference between what you’re experiencing symbolically and normal reality. This isn’t something to deal with in hypnosis.

The general rule is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”: if what you're doing is making you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, or things feel more and more unreal, stop going deeper and get help.
section: Could It Be Psychosis? (Appendix H: Demons, Jinn & Presences)
reader: Someone who met what feels like a hostile presence (a demon, a jinn, a mocking or hateful voice) in hypnosis, meditation, prayer or another altered state, has read the appendix's ways to ground themselves and close the door on it, and now wonders whether what is happening to them is psychosis or their mind coming loose, and whether to carry on or get help.

sentences.s: Everything above assumes that the “hostile presence” is symbolic, the kind that settles down when you ground yourself and meet it with love.
What you’re going through might instead be psychosis, or your mind becoming unstable in some other way.
Get help right away if you feel under attack for days at a time, or you can’t sleep or function normally.
The same goes if you hear voices telling you to do things, feel you need to hurt yourself or somebody else, or feel you’re going manic.
And get help if you can’t communicate normally, or can’t tell the difference between what you’re experiencing symbolically and normal reality.
This isn’t something to deal with in hypnosis.

The general rule is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”: if what you're doing is making you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, or things feel more and more unreal, stop going deeper and get help.
sentences.payoff: They get the rule for the case the urgent list above doesn't cover: no single alarming sign yet, but what they are doing is making them more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, or less sure what is real. Then they stop going deeper and get help, without waiting until it is days of feeling attacked, or voices. The section's name tells them where the guide gives the rule whole, with the signs that it is fine to carry on gently.
sentences.follows: The paragraph before lists the particular signs for getting help right away and ends 'This isn't something to deal with in hypnosis'. This gives the general rule after those particular cases, for a change the reader notices over time and not a state they are already in, so it comes last.

checked.point: the general rule is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”
checked.found: That section (the h1 before the Closing, in AFTER.md) gives the same rule in other words: if you find yourself more loving, honest, functional, relational, grounded, 'keep on keeping on gently'; 'If you notice that your ordinary life is becoming less stable, don't try to go deeper', then more sleep, eating, grounding, boundaries and support. It does not list paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, and it says 'more support from other people' where this says 'get help'. Those words are the author's, from 'The General Rule' passage this sentence replaces (HIS-S143.txt).
checked.still_needed: yes: they act on the half of the rule kept here, which is the half for their case, and follow the link when they want the other half: what it looks like when the practice is doing them good, and what to do for steadiness (sleep, food, grounding, boundaries, support)

placement: Last paragraph of 'Could It Be Psychosis?', where the author's 'The General Rule' stood as an h3 under this section: after the urgent get-help signs and 'This isn't something to deal with in hypnosis', before the heading 'Cosmic-Download Test'. It stays with the appendix's other get-help text, and comes after the particular signs because it is the general case of them. Its first words, 'The general rule', point back at those signs (when to stop and get help); 'the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”' points to the section of that name before the Closing, which will be a link and holds the rule's other half. It has no 'also', 'this' or 'as for'.

opens.first_sentence: Everything above assumes that the “hostile presence” is symbolic, the kind that settles down when you ground yourself and meet it with love.
opens.why_reading: It gives the reader the test for their own case: everything above (grounding, compassion, closing the door) was for a presence 'that settles down when you ground yourself and meet it with love'. If theirs hasn't settled, they see at once that this section is about them, and read on for what it might be instead and what to do.

same_point: Read the section from its heading to the next. Paragraph 2 gives the urgent signs, and two of them come again in this sentence as a direction: 'can't sleep' and 'more ... sleepless'; 'can't tell the difference between what you're experiencing symbolically and normal reality' and 'things feel more and more unreal'. Both places stay: paragraph 2 is 'right away' for a state the reader is already in, and this sentence is the rule for a change that what they are doing is making, with 'stop going deeper'. The rule's other half (more loving, more grounded ... keep doing it gently) was said twice in the guide, here under its own h3 and in 'Daily Life Is the Feedback': the h3 and that half are deleted here, and this one sentence links to the section that keeps them.

needed.reader: a fresh reader (subagent, 2026-11-25), given tools/humanization/needed_read_brief.md with the section, its heading and what it is for: the reader is about to decide whether what they are going through is past what this guide's practices can handle, and to stop and get help if it is

needs.S1: to know the advice above was for a presence that settles with grounding and love, so they can test theirs against it
needs.S2: to have the other possibility named: psychosis, or the mind becoming unstable
needs.S3-S5: the signs for getting help right away, each one something they can check in themselves
needs.S6: to stop trying to handle such a state with the practice itself
needs.S7: the rule for when none of those signs is there yet but what they are doing is making them worse by degrees: stop going deeper and get help; and where the whole rule is

his_fixes.reader: a fresh reader (subagent, 2026-11-25), given tools/humanization/his_fixes_brief.md and the text one sentence a line (what it is for: deciding whether this is past the guide's practices, and getting help). The author's own six sentences were read as the text around the new one and are not marked.

marked.s: The general rule is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”: if what you're doing is making you more paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated or scared, or things feel more and more unreal, stop going deeper and get help.
marked.difference: 11, mild: it says where the rule lives ('is the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”') before the rule itself; his way gives what the reader gets first and its source after. Nothing else: it ends on what to do, it connects ('The general rule' after the particular signs), and each sign is named.

kept.The general rule is the one in “Daily Li: He read this exact sentence on his picks page and answered 'ok' (answer 7, 2026-11-25 01:08 UTC), after asking for the passage to be 'cut and link' (2026-11-24). 'The general rule' says in its first three words what the reader is getting; the section's name is seven words and tells them where these changes show, in daily life, before the list of them; and what follows the colon is his own half of the rule, word for word. A rule-first alternative is in the subagent's report to the editor, for him to take or leave.

fit.reader: a fresh reader (subagent, 2026-11-25), given tools/humanization/fit_read_brief.md. WHAT IT IS: a section of an appendix to a self-hypnosis guide, for people who meet what feels like a hostile presence in an altered state. YOUR MOMENT: I have felt such a presence, I have read how to ground myself and close the door on it, and I am deciding whether this could be psychosis and whether to get help.
fit.note: Read for ANYWAY on 'scared': anyone who has just met such a presence is frightened. Not marked, because the line says 'making you more ... scared', a direction that what they are doing is producing, and the section it names puts that in daily life; one fright is not that. The list is the author's own.

questions.Q1: PASS: 'The general rule is' tells the reader in three words why they are reading the sentence (after the particular signs, the rule they are cases of), and the instruction, 'stop going deeper and get help', ends it as it does in the author's wording. The section's name stands before the rule itself; the read against his fixes marked that as mild and it is kept with the reason there. No term is explained late: none in the sentence needs explaining.
questions.Q2: PASS: the one instruction, 'stop going deeper and get help', is something the reader does, and the clause before it says what it is for: what they are doing is making them worse.
questions.Q3: PASS: the signs are named one by one (paranoid, sleepless, grandiose, isolated, scared, things feeling more and more unreal), not 'if it gets worse'; the place is named by its heading, not 'see above' or 'elsewhere in the guide'.
questions.Q4: PASS: 'the one in “Daily Life Is the Feedback”' is the rule in the section of that name, which will be a link; 'what you're doing' is the practice the reader is in (the sentence before ends 'in hypnosis'); 'going deeper' is the guide's own word for more trance or more of the same practice. No term here is beyond a high-school graduate; 'psychosis' is in the author's second sentence, where the section first uses it.
questions.Q5: PASS: it follows the list of urgent signs as the general case after the particular ones ('The general rule'); 'the one' is 'rule' in the same sentence; the 'if' has its act in the same sentence.
questions.Q6: PASS: the urgent signs first ('right away'), then that this isn't for hypnosis, then the wider rule for what builds up over time: most urgent first, and the place the author's own 'General Rule' had.
questions.Q7: PASS: the half of the rule kept here is the half for this reader's case (the practice may be unsettling them); the half about carrying on gently when it is doing them good was cut from here and stays in the linked section.
questions.Q8: PASS: the section now has two sets of signs, 'get help right away' (paragraph 2) and the general rule's. Sleeplessness and unreality are in both, and belong in both: paragraph 2 names the state (can't sleep; can't tell symbolic from normal reality), the rule names the direction (more sleepless; more and more unreal), and both end in 'get help', so no sign is given two different answers.
questions.Q9: PASS: one condition and one instruction, with the small words in place ('if what you're doing is making you more ...', 'or things feel ...', 'and get help').

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
